description: Surveys are perhaps the most ubiquitous tool that organizations, institutions, and companies can use to gather information about a population of interest. The purpose of this course is to provide a foundation and introduction to survey design and analytic skills needed to analyze the data collected from the survey. Along with relevant statistical concepts including variable types, distributions, and sampling methods this course will explore the process of designing surveys establishing the purpose of a survey, understanding the process of item writing, minimizing measurement error, piloting items and surveys and how to report and disseminate our findings to support the survey purpose. Prerequisite: SDS 272 and SDS 164 or permission of instructor.
